title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). We have a smooth connected S over a field K of finite type over Q, with k the algebraic closure of Q in K. Over S there is a family of motives. G is its motivic Galois group over Q, a Tannakian-type group. P is the G-torsor of fibre functors (de Rham against Betti), carrying the integrable Gauss–Manin connection. i_1 and i_2 are the two Hodge cocharacters, with central weight cocharacter i = i_1 i_2. w : π_1(S(C), ξ) → G(Q) is the monodromy. α is the comparison (period) point of P at the base point ξ.

On this page Grothendieck adds the transcendental (Hodge-theoretic) structure, i.e. the period map in group-theoretic form.
(1) Take the universal cover S̄_C of the connected component of ξ in S(C), with marked point ξ̄.
(2) Take 𝒴_G, the set of homomorphisms h : 𝕊 = Res_{C/R} G_m → G_R whose weight is the given central cocharacter i. This is a union of G(R)-conjugacy classes, i.e. a Mumford–Tate / Shimura-type domain. It is viewed as a complex manifold on which G(R), hence G(Q), acts.
(3) Postulate a map f : S̄_C → 𝒴_G with three properties:
  12a) f(ξ̄) is the Hodge homomorphism given by i_1^C and i_2^C.
  12b) f is equivariant: f(g s̄) = w(g) f(s̄) for g in π_1.
  12c) f is holomorphic.
(4) Item 14, added later, 'modulo Hodge'. The composite S̄_C → 𝒴_G → 𝒴_{G̃} is constant. Here G̃ = G/R and R is the algebraic group generated by the monodromy image. By 12b the composite a priori only factors through S(C)°.
(5) Item 13 is compatibility with the algebraic structure. If s̄ lies over a point t of S (S shrunk so that P with its connection is defined over S), then f(s̄)_C : 𝕊_C → (G_{k(t)})_C ≅ G_C defines the Hodge bigrading on G-modules. This bigrading is compatible with the torsor P_t, its Hodge filtration, and the C-trivialisation p(s̄). Here p : S̄_C → (P_S)^an_C is the horizontal (flat) section of the analytic connection fixed by p(ξ̄) = α.

In modern terms this is the period map of a variation of Hodge structure, lifted to the universal cover, equivariant for monodromy, with values in the Mumford–Tate-type domain of the motivic Galois group. The point of item 14, used on the next page, is that the Hodge structure projected to G/(algebraic monodromy) is constant. This feeds the conjectural descent of P/R, with its connection, filtration and Hodge cocharacters, to the field of constants k: a motivic 'theorem of the fixed part'.
errors: Numbering is out of order (12, 14, 13): item 14 was inserted afterwards and replaces a crossed-out formulation about the smallest R-algebraic subgroup containing f(s̄)(𝕊).

𝒴_G as 'all homomorphisms with given weight' is generally a disjoint union of G(R)-conjugacy classes. Its complex structure has to be specified (the flag-variety embedding via the Hodge filtration); this is left implicit.

Griffiths transversality of f is not stated; only holomorphy is. It is perhaps implicit in item 13 through compatibility with the integrable connection and the filtration, but it is not made explicit.

Item 14 depends on the Hodge conjecture to identify the motivic group with the Mumford–Tate group, and implicitly on R being normal in G. The next page says normality comes from item 9 (normality of the geometric monodromy image), so it is assumed rather than proved here.

ideas.what: Hodge structures encoded as homomorphisms from Res_{C/R} G_m into G_R with fixed central weight cocharacter, forming a homogeneous complex domain acted on by G(R) and G(Q)
ideas.modern_name: Deligne torus 𝕊, Mumford–Tate domains / Shimura data (G, X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971, Théorie de Hodge II 1971); Mumford (1966); Green–Griffiths–Kerr for Mumford–Tate domains

ideas.what: Period map from the universal cover into this domain, equivariant for the monodromy representation and holomorphic, normalised at the base point
ideas.modern_name: Period map of a variation of Hodge structure (Griffiths)

ideas.what: Projection of the period map to G/R, R = algebraic monodromy group, is constant (modulo Hodge)
ideas.modern_name: Theorem of the fixed part; normality of algebraic monodromy in the generic Mumford–Tate group

ideas.what: Period torsor trivialisation p as a horizontal analytic section of P with p(ξ̄)=α, compatible with the Hodge bigrading at each point
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of periods / Gauss–Manin flat section; motivic Galois group as stabiliser of periods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, via André), Deligne, Katz–Oda
ideas.where_published: Period conjecture mentioned in Lang's Introduction to Transcendental Numbers (1966), attributed to Grothendieck

missed.claim: Already by 1965 Grothendieck parametrises variations of motivic Hodge structure by an equivariant holomorphic map from the universal cover into the space of homomorphisms Res_{C/R}G_m → G_R of fixed weight, with G the motivic Galois group. This is essentially the Deligne-torus / Mumford–Tate-domain formalism, predating Deligne 1971 and Griffiths' period domains in this group-theoretic form.
missed.quote: Soit 𝒴_G l'ensemble des hom. de 𝕊=∏_{C/R} G_{m,C} dans G_R, correspondant à l'hom. central i ... f: S̄_C → 𝒴_G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: it shows the 𝕊-formalism and Mumford–Tate domains were at least partly Grothendieck's, inside a motivic Galois setting.

missed.claim: The fixed-part statement is formulated motivically: the Hodge structure modulo monodromy is constant, and (next page) the quotient torsor P/R with connection, filtration and Hodge cocharacters descends to the field of constants k. This anticipates André's normality theorem and his motivic 'deformation principle'. The full descent statement for motivic Galois groups remains conjectural.
missed.quote: 14) (Moyennant Hodge) Le composé S̄_C → 𝒴_G → 𝒴_{G̃} ... est une application ... constante.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an early precise formulation of a motivic fixed-part / descent conjecture, relevant to André's motivated cycles and to arithmetic descent of variations.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas are now standard (Deligne torus, Mumford–Tate domains, fixed-part theorem, André normality), but seeing them assembled by Grothendieck in 1965 for the motivic Galois group is a notable unpublished historical detail. The page contains no unknown mathematics.
transcription_corrections: In 12b the coefficient is most likely w(g) (the monodromy w used on the next page), written over a correction, not ρ(g): f(g s̄) = w(g) f(s̄).
The symbol for the domain is a script gamma-like letter (𝒱 or 𝒴); it is used consistently as 𝒴_G and 𝒴_{G̃}.
In 12a the inserted words are 'point marqué de S̄_C' and the reference is 'défini par i_1^C, i_2^C de c)'.
In 13 the phrase is 'P comme torseur à connexion intégr. P_S soit défini sur S' and later '(d'une filtration)' annotates 'l'hom'. The word read as 'intégrable' before f(s̄)_C is uncertain.
The last line reads 'p(s̄) [p : S̄_C → (P_S)^an_C ... par les conditions que p(ξ̄) = α]'.
